selection: Ten widely recognised classics, curated from Polish cultural and food references; not a measured national ranking.
notes: All ten cooking sources are Polish Feast. Titles, descriptions and methods are independently written in English. No images or blog prose imported.

Metric equivalents printed by the source take precedence. Otherwise pounds convert to grams rounded to the nearest gram; cups and spoons remain source measures without guessed densities. Unspecified quantities remain null and numeric ranges are retained.
Timing uses source recipe-card metadata except pickle soup (30–32 min from the method) and barley soup (2 hr from its sequential method; card says 1 hr 40 min).
Beet soup prep includes stock preparation and parallel beet boiling; cook includes the final five-minute simmer. Its required six-hour refrigerated rest is explicit.
Tomato and white soup cards give longer cook times than their methods; retain those allowances and require fully cooked meat. Raw-meat washing instructions are omitted.
Rye and white soup use prepared fermented soup starters; white soup uses the source bottled-base option. Starter fermentation is not included in cooking time.

Water omitted from split pea and white soup ingredient lists is included from their methods. Optional serving ingredients are explicit; an unspecified piece of celery root is not assigned an invented weight.
Mushroom recipe uses fresh mushrooms as the main option; the dried alternative is expressed as a scalable one-tenth weight.
